title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
summary:
The GoAhead embedded web server loaded a certificate revocation list into its default TLS backend but never turned revocation checking on, so a revoked client certificate could still pass login on affected setups.

title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
summary:
Apple on Monday backported fixes for a high-severity security flaw that was exploited in real-world cyber attacks to older devices.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 (CVSS score: 8.8), is an out-of-bounds write affecting CoreGraphics that could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted file.

title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Permissionless Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens
summary:
Microsoft has fixed a flaw in its Authenticator app for Android that let a malicious app with no permissions pose as a trusted Microsoft app, such as Teams, and collect sign-in tokens for a victim's work account.

title: Keystone to Destroy 18,835 Hardware Wallets After Hackers Steal Device Verification Key
summary:

summary:

title: Australia Gets Into Amadey Malware Backend, Cuts Off Access to 180,000 Infected Computers
summary:
A criminal using the Amadey malware can no longer access or steal data from 180,000 infected computers around the world, including some in Australia, the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) says. The agency's operators gained access to the criminal's operation's backend and cut it off from those computers.
